query: Does remote-first work increase or decrease engineering productivity in mid-size SaaS companies (2020-2026)?
bottom_line: Remote-first engineering productivity is highly sensitive to measurement definition: output-ticket studies often show flat-to-positive effects, while collaboration-and-innovation proxies more often show modest declines. Treat a single-direction answer as over-specified.

research_questions.question: How is engineering productivity defined across studies (commits, cycle time, revenue/FTE, self-report)?
What causal or quasi-experimental evidence exists for remote-first vs office-first engineering teams?
Do effects differ by seniority, company size, or time since remote transition?
Which findings replicate across independent datasets rather than the same firm sample?
What are the strongest disconfirming findings?

sources.title: Work from Home and Productivity: Evidence from Patent and Firm Data
sources.author: Bloom et al.
sources.methodology: Difference-in-differences on firm patent output and inventor location with matched controls and robustness to alternative clustering.
sources.limitations: Patent counts lag real-time engineering throughput; US-heavy sample.

claims.claim: Remote-first work increases engineering ticket throughput in mid-size SaaS firms.
Remote-first work decreases engineering collaboration quality and innovation proxies.
Measured labour productivity at national level is mixed and not occupation-specific.
Cycle-time meta-analysis finds a small negative remote effect that is significant.
Cycle-time studies find remote work is ineffective at improving delivery speed.
Senior engineers benefit more from remote-first than juniors.

findings.text: Productivity results flip with the metric: throughput and individual output often look better; collaboration, mentoring, and patent/innovation proxies often look worse.
Vendor surveys overstate positive remote effects relative to official statistics and peer-reviewed syntheses.
Heterogeneity by seniority is plausible but currently single-lineage in this packet.

analysis: Do not collapse 'productivity' into one number. Ticket throughput, cycle time, and innovation output are different constructs.
Shared-lineage risk is moderate: several papers cite the same NBER working paper.
Low-integrity blogs are retained only as narrative illustration of the public debate.
disagreements: Throughput-positive vs cycle-time-negative results are a factual-metric dispute, not a values dispute.
limitations: Sample notes are illustrative and use placeholder URLs.
Occupation-specific causal designs remain thin outside a few firm panels.
recommended_actions: Define the decision metric before citing any productivity study.
Discount vendor surveys unless corroborated by official statistics or peer-reviewed syntheses.
Commission or locate a seniority-split replication before using that claim in policy.
decision_framework: If the goal is individual ticket output: remote-first is not clearly harmful.
If the goal is mentoring density and invention: budget for in-person collaboration, especially for juniors.
